title: fix(driver-sql): a date field still on a Postgres timestamptz column reads the day it was written
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D2jPwcqa1xjmHhfHrDAv2ri)_

Fixes #32851

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:Postgres 上把日期时间字段改成日期字段并发布后,该列仍是 `timestamptz`;现在这种字段的写入、读取、按日期过滤、按天分组统一按 UTC 日计算,四处答案一致。列类型不动,存量数据不改写。
- 为什么改:数据库服务器时区在 UTC 以东(如上海)时,写入 2026-11-12 读回是 2026-11-11,且按日期过滤、按天分组各给出不同的日子,用户看到的日期整体早一天,没有任何报错。
- 风险与回滚:只影响"Postgres + 日期字段 + 列仍是 timestamptz"这一种组合;日期时间字段、SQLite、MySQL 的行为不变。修复前已经写进去的错误日子保持原样(仍早一天),本 PR 不修数据。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/date-on-instant-column.ts`(规则与理由),其次 `sql-driver-rotation.ts` 里登记哪些列是 timestamptz 的那段,再看 `sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts` 的 `filterColumnExpr` 新分支。
- 两分钟验证:`OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=… TZ=America/New_York pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql exec vitest run src/sql-driver-32851-date-on-instant-column.test.ts`(服务器时区设为 Asia/Shanghai),预期 Postgres 与 SQLite 两格全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

Chosen shape: **(b), read every door in a fixed zone (UTC)**, not (a), narrowing the column.

- New module `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/date-on-instant-column.ts`: the registry type, the predicate `isDateOnInstantColumn`, the write binding `utcMidnightOfDay` and the SQL `utcCalendarDaySql` (`((col) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date`), with the measurement and the reasoning in its header.
- `SqlDriver.dateFieldsOnInstantColumn` (protected registry): per table, the declared `Field.date` fields whose Postgres column is `timestamp with time zone`. `initObjects` (the call `syncSchema` and the publish's storage sync make) records it from the `columnInfo()` it already reads for an existing table; it is reset to empty for every table it syncs, so a table created here, a non-Postgres dialect, deferred DDL or a guest datasource keeps the plain `date` path exactly as before.
- Write (`formatInput`): such a field binds the day as its UTC midnight (`2026-11-12T00:00:00.000Z`) instead of the bare day the server read in its own zone. This is the Oracle arm's rule (`oracleDayBinding`).
- Filter (`filterColumnExpr`, so every comparison operator, the object shorthand, cross-field and now-anchor comparisons) and the outside-the-builder twin `temporalFilterColumnSql` (analytics native SQL): the column is read as its UTC calendar day; the comparand stays the `YYYY-MM-DD` day it already was.
- Date bucket (`buildDateBucketExpr`, so `aggregate()` and the `dateBucketSql` echo): such a field buckets as its UTC calendar day instead of `::date` in the session zone.
- Read: unchanged. It already folds the stored instant by its UTC components (`temporalStorageForm`), which is the zone every other door now uses.

Why (b) and not (a):

- (a) narrows only "when that loses nothing", which is only an empty column or one whose every value is a UTC midnight. The card's own case is a live object: rows written while the field was a `datetime` carry a time of day, and rows written after the publish on a server ahead of UTC are stored at 16:00Z of the previous day. Narrowing those changes stored values, which the order routes to `needs_decision`; skipping them leaves the defect in place. So (a) alone does not fix the reported case, and once (b) is in, (a) adds nothing.
- (b) changes no stored value and no column, makes all four doors agree for every stored value (including a row written as a `datetime` before the publish, which a comparand-only fix would still miss), and leaves `datetime` fields untouched.
- A session-wide `TimeZone = UTC` on every Postgres connection (the MySQL `withUtcSession` shape) was considered and rejected as wider: it moves every raw statement and host query on the pool, and it still would not make an equality filter match a stored instant with a time of day.

Existing rows: a day written into such a column **before** this fix, on a server ahead of UTC, was stored as the previous day's instant (`2026-11-11T16:00:00Z` for `2026-11-12`). It keeps reading, filtering and bucketing as that previous day, now consistently. It is not repaired: from the column alone it cannot be told apart from a `datetime`-era value at the same instant, so a repair needs a data migration and a decision (see Acceptance notes). Rows written while the field was a `datetime` read, filter and bucket as their UTC day.

## Tests

- New `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-32851-date-on-instant-column.test.ts`, on every dialect cell of the live matrix (SQLite always; Postgres and MySQL where provisioned, which the `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` job does with both servers at `Asia/Shanghai` and the process at `America/New_York`). It creates the table with `due: datetime`, writes a `datetime`-era row (`2026-11-12T20:00:00Z`, 04:00 the next day in Shanghai), publishes `due: date` through `syncSchema` + `applyPublishedColumnChanges`, then:
  - Postgres premise: the column is still `timestamptz` and the server's offset is ahead of UTC (fails, with a remedy, if the server is at UTC);
  - every cell: `create({ due: '2026-11-12' })` answers and reads `2026-11-12`, an `update` to that day reads it back, `due = day` and `$gte/$lte day` find both, `$lt day` does not;
  - every cell: a `datetime` field beside it (`seen`) still reads and filters as its exact instant;
  - Postgres: the `datetime`-era row reads `2026-11-12`, the equality filter returns all three rows, and `aggregate()` by day answers one bucket `2026-11-12` of 3;
  - Postgres: `temporalFilterColumnSql` + `temporalFilterValue`, and the `dateBucketSql` echo, answer the same.

<details><summary>Pre-fix measurement on main (b4f69716), live Postgres 16 at Asia/Shanghai, TZ=America/New_York</summary>

```text
col timestamp with time zone Asia/Shanghai America/New_York
create answers 2026-11-11
raw [{"due":"2026-11-12 21:00:00+08"} (datetime-era), {"due":"2026-11-12 00:00:00+08"} (written as 2026-11-12)]
read a 2026-11-12 read b 2026-11-11
filter eq ["b"]
filter range ["b"]
bucket [{"due":"2026-11-12","n":2}]
```

After the fix: `create answers 2026-11-12`, stored `2026-11-12 08:00:00+08` (UTC midnight), both rows read `2026-11-12`, `filter eq ["a","b"]`, bucket `2026-11-12` of 2.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (each leg through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs; restore verified blob == HEAD and git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

```text
registry population removed (sql-driver-rotation.ts)   exit 1 · 3 failed: read-back ("2026-11-12" expected, "2026-11-11" received), datetime-era row, analytics doors
write binding removed (sql-driver-sqlite-serialisation.ts) exit 1 · 4 failed: read-back ("2026-11-11"), filter, datetime-era row, analytics doors
filterColumnExpr arm removed (sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts) exit 1 · 2 failed: filter by day, datetime-era row
date bucket arm removed (sql-driver-date-bucket.ts)      exit 1 · 2 failed: datetime-era row bucket, dateBucketSql echo
temporalFilterColumnSql arm removed (sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts) exit 1 · 1 failed: analytics doors
```

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Days already written into such a column before this fix on a server ahead of UTC stay one day early (now consistently on every door). Repairing them needs a data migration that shifts values by the server's offset, and only rows written after the publish need it, which the column cannot tell apart. Not done here; the seat can raise it as a decision if wanted.
- Found, not fixed (pre-existing, every dialect, unrelated to time zones): on SQLite and MySQL a row written while the field was a `datetime` (an instant with a time of day) reads as its day but is not matched by an equality filter on that day, because the comparand is the bare day and the column holds the instant. Postgres now matches it through the UTC-day column read. Reported to the seat in the os-dev report.
- The registry is filled by the schema sync. A driver that never syncs the table (deferred DDL on `os migrate plan`, a guest datasource with `schemaMode` other than managed) keeps the pre-fix behaviour for such a column.
- A `timestamp without time zone` column under a `date` field is not recorded: this driver never builds one for a `datetime` field.
- An index on such a column no longer serves a filter on the field (the column is read through an expression). Only columns left by a publish that changed a field from `datetime` to `date` are affected.

All 72 exit 0.
- `--ran` reconciliation at `6c557952`: ✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 70 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
- The first pass at `583b1e38` was green except `check:query-options-erasure` (the new test cast six query bags `as any`); `6c557952` types them and the full union was re-run on it.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql test` with live Postgres 16 (server `Asia/Shanghai`, `TZ=America/New_York`): 261 files passed, 4 skipped; 5319 tests passed, 122 skipped (run at `89ffef34`, same driver-sql source as the final head except the pin's casts; the pin re-run on `6c557952`: 9 passed, 4 skipped).

- Dogfood battery: not owed (no `!` in the title, `Clause-②: no` without a narrowing arm).
